author: agent
text: Schema boundary is load-bearing: field names (shape_hash, logic_hash, etc.) are persisted to .coord/index/*.json and cannot be renamed without breaking index compatibility. Private function names (_shape_hash, _logic_hash) can be renamed freely. Changing persisted fields requires migration or re-initialization, which loses accumulated metadata. The .coord directory holds unrecoverable knowledge across refactors.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.55.2 and still exact. Verified against the artifact rather than the source: .coord/index/coordinates.json persists 20 keys per entity and shape_hash, logic_hash and body_hash are all among them, so the schema boundary this note draws is real - renaming those fields does break index compatibility. The complement holds too: no private name leaks into the persisted rows (zero keys beginning with underscore), so _shape_hash/_logic_hash remain free to rename, exactly as claimed. 0.55.1 added the compact sketch encoding and moved the parse cache without disturbing any of this; the hash moved with that release and this is the first re-read since.
